description:
A contemporary, leakage-audited corpus for web-application injection-attack detection: 61,400 labelled HTTP requests across three deliberately vulnerable practice applications and fourteen attack families, with fixed payload-disjoint and template-disjoint splits and an automated 32-check quality gate that fails the build if a known shortcut or label leak reappears.

Every attack request is the counterfactual twin of a benign request differing only by the injected span, so the payload can be deleted surgically and attribution becomes a measurement rather than an estimate. The build is deterministic and seeded, every released file is checksummed in SHA256SUMS, and the repository ships a datasheet together with every result file the accompanying paper reports.

This is the archived artefact for the ICISSP 2027 paper Injection-Deletion Ablation: A Leakage-Audited Corpus for Web Application Injection Detection.

Code is licensed MIT; the dataset is licensed CC BY 4.0. Attack payloads derive from PayloadsAllTheThings (MIT); see NOTICE. All benign traffic is synthetic and contains no real users, credentials or personal data.
